data.note: pure research doc, independent of tool-diet; forced past inherited phase dependency

data.text:
Does Kilo CLI 7.8.12 re-fetch tools/list on notifications/tools/list_changed (immediate and unsolicited-idle) and can the model use a tool it was not told the name of?
Kilo 7.8.12 re-issues tools/list within 30 ms of an immediate list_changed and also after an idle one sent 6 s after the call returned; the new tool secret_oracle is then found and called. It negotiates initialize 2025-11-25 (clientInfo kilo/7.8.12, capabilities.roots only) and exposes MCP tools to the model through an execute tool (tools.lc.x).
Kilo/opencode lineage registers a ToolListChangedNotificationSchema handler that rebuilds s.defs and publishes ToolsChanged (Kilo-Org/kilocode packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts:555-583).

Which open-source MCP clients have a tools/list_changed handler that refreshes the model-visible tool set (opencode, Gemini CLI, Codex, Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, Cline, Roo, Goose, Continue, OpenHands, Zed, VS Code Copilot, superagent grok-cli, Aider)?
By source reading (no probe): honour = opencode, Gemini CLI, VS Code Copilot, Cline (restarts the whole session), Goose, OpenHands, Zed; ignore = Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, Roo, Continue (commented-out TODO), superagent grok-cli; Codex has the handler behind feature mcp_tool_list_changed (UnderDevelopment, default off); Aider has no MCP client. Only opencode/Gemini/Cline/VS Code re-list prompts. Revisions: Codex legacy 2025-06-18 (2026-07-28 behind flag), Goose Auto prefers 2026-07-28, opencode SDK 2.0.0 knows it, VS Code and Zed 2025-11-25, Roo SDK 1.12.0.
Handlers registered through setNotificationHandler / SDK listChanged options; negative cells come from greps that find none, which is evidence not proof; shipped releases may lag the default branch.

What is known about list_changed, caching and reconnect for the closed-source or doc-only clients: Cursor IDE/CLI, Copilot CLI, Antigravity, Grok Build, Windsurf, Amp, Factory Droid?
Cursor CLI ignores tools/list_changed until restart (forum 161459); Cursor IDE staff say the cache is intentional and list_changed regressed in 3.12.17 for non-stdio servers, only a full restart is guaranteed (forum 166216, 2026-08-25). Copilot CLI, Antigravity, Grok Build, Windsurf, Amp and Droid: docs are silent on list_changed (UNKNOWN); Grok Build and Antigravity refresh manually; Copilot CLI recovers cached tools on tool-list refresh and applies config changes between turns (changelog 1.0.101). No project named grokbot was found; superagent-ai/grok-cli has no handler.
Closed clients can only be classified by docs, trackers or a probe; without a probe the safe default is ignore (hard upgrade).

data.summary: 'ddflow research add --id R-x --verdict CONFIRMED --relation extends:R-parent' returns id R-parent and appends the text as an 'addition' to the parent; R-x is never created, the parent keeps its old verdict (THEORETICAL even after a CONFIRMED probe), and the chosen id cannot be cited. Either create the note and link it, or let an addition carry its own verdict.

data.summary: 'ddflow session prompt "text"' fails: first argument is taken as the session id and needs --text; the MCP ddflow_session_prompt finds the latest open session implicitly. Make the CLI take the text positionally or default the session, so subagents without MCP can record the operator's words.

data.body:
Add to each harness descriptor: list_changed = honours|ignores|unknown, verified_version, source. Seed: claude honours (2.1.296, R-soft-claude-listchanged), cursor ignores (forum 161459), others unknown (= hard). Keyed by clientInfo.name/version from the connection. A `ddflow mcp probe-client` (adapting the scratchpad srv.py) lets an operator verify any client and write the result. Prompts list_changed stays unknown until probed outside -p mode.

Client matrix (SU-client-matrix, docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md): seed ALL rows with evidence tag + verified_version/date, not only claude and cursor. honours: claude 2.1.296 (VERIFIED), kilo 7.8.12 (VERIFIED), opencode, gemini, vscode-copilot, cline, goose, openhands, zed (SOURCE). ignores: qwen, kimi, roo, continue, grok-cli (SOURCE), cursor-cli (REPORTED), cursor IDE unreliable (REPORTED, stdio maybe ok), codex (feature flag off by default; SOURCE). n/a: aider (no MCP). unknown: copilot-cli, antigravity, grok build, windsurf, amp, droid. Key by clientInfo.name + version range (Cursor changed between builds). Add a tri-state source: verified|source|reported|observed (learned at runtime by SU-announce's acknowledgement wait). Unknown = hard. Only additions/removals count as honoured: Claude Code does not adopt a changed schema of a loaded tool. prompts/list_changed is never relied on.

On a swap whose digest changed: set listChanged true for tools and prompts; emit notifications/tools/list_changed and prompts/list_changed on legacy revisions, serve subscriptions/listen on 2026-07-28 (opt-in types), and replace the fixed 1 h tools/list ttlMs with a short one plus the digest so cached lists converge. Debounce and coalesce. Only when the client is known to honour it (SU-client-table); else classify hard.

Client matrix: (1) only tools/list_changed is announced for correctness; prompts/resources are best effort (few clients re-list prompts). (2) Observed acknowledgement: after sending list_changed the shim waits N s for a tools/list from that client; a re-fetch records the (clientInfo name, version) as honours/observed in the client table, silence records ignores and returns a hard verdict with the restart notice (SU-restart-notice). (3) 2026-07-28 clients (Codex/Goose/opencode can negotiate it): short ttlMs keyed to the digest. (4) Cline answers by restarting its session, so debounce/coalesce bursts.

After `ddflow upgrade --apply` (and on the periodic stale check) classify with SU-digest and act: SOFT -> swap the worker and print 'soft upgrade applied, no restart needed (interface unchanged | N tools added, M removed: announced to <client>)'; HARD -> 'hard upgrade: restart your agent' with the reason (shim changed / protocol changed / client <name> does not refresh tools). New [mcp].upgrade = soft|notify|off, default soft where classification allows; keep on_upgrade=reexec as the hard-upgrade path that avoids a client reconnect when the shim itself is stable. doctor shows running vs installed versions, class of the pending upgrade, client capability. Same text on CLI, MCP footer and the SessionStart hook.

Rule (docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md): SOFT iff digest unchanged OR (change is additive/removal AND client honours list_changed: table verified/source or observed ack) OR facade mode on (SU-facade-mode; the digest then covers only the facade tools + instructions). A schema change of an existing tool is soft only with the worker grace (previous schema accepted for one version) AND an honouring client; else HARD. Otherwise HARD with the reason naming the client. The report names the mode used (unchanged | announced to <client> | facade). Needs SU-facade-mode and SU-restart-notice.

Present R-soft-* and the recommendation; settle: (1) A+D over B/C-only, (2) worker transport: stdio pipes to a child (default, portable incl. Windows) vs unix socket, (3) the soft/hard definition in the phase body, (4) schema grace: worker accepts the previous schema's arguments for one version, (5) what happens for clients that ignore list_changed (hard, tell the user). Record with ddflow decision add --globs ddflow/mcpshim/**,ddflow/surfaces/mcp*.py. Do not start SU-shim before this is decided.

Item (5) revised by the client matrix: clients that ignore list_changed are not simply hard. Decide: facade mode (ddflow_search/ddflow_call, MTD-search-call) as the way to make upgrades soft for them, the per-call restart notice as the fallback, and the rule 'soft iff digest unchanged OR client honours OR facade on'. See docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md.

Pure function: canonical digest of tools/list (per profile from MTD-profiles), prompts, instructions template, capabilities, protocol versions; plus classify(old, new, client_caps) -> soft|hard with reasons (additive, removed, schema-compatible, required-arg change, shim protocol change). Golden tests, deterministic ordering (the 2026-07-28 spec asks for it). Per-profile digests since profiles change the list.

Digest is computed per exposed surface: flat tools, a profile, or facade mode (only ddflow_search/ddflow_call + instructions). classify() takes client capability (honours|ignores|unknown) and facade flag, returns soft|hard with reasons; changed schema of an existing tool is its own reason (client may keep old args: Claude Code VERIFIED).

From the client matrix: Qwen, Kimi, Roo, Continue, Cursor, Codex (default) and probably others never refresh the tool list. With the MTD-search-call facade the client sees 2-3 tools whose names, descriptions and schemas never change; the backend operations live behind ddflow_call and ddflow_search reads the live set, so a worker swap needs no client-visible change. Config [mcp].surface = flat|profile|facade (default flat; facade chosen automatically for clients in the table marked ignores/unknown when [mcp].auto_facade). Digest covers the facade only. Tests: swap a worker that adds an operation under a client that ignores list_changed; ddflow_search finds it, ddflow_call runs it, no notification sent. Cost: accuracy (MTD-accuracy-eval).
data.title: Facade mode: stable ddflow_search/ddflow_call surface makes worker swaps soft for clients that ignore list_changed

data.body: The shim remembers the digest it served in the connection's last tools/list. When the worker digest differs and the client is not known to honour list_changed (or did not acknowledge), append a one-line footer to tool results: 'ddflow was upgraded (N tools added, M changed): restart your agent to see them' (rate limited, once per N calls and once per session start); a call to a removed tool returns the same message instead of a bare 'no such tool'. Same text as ddflow doctor and the SessionStart hook.
data.title: Restart-required notice in tool results when a hard upgrade is pending for this client

data.body: Productise the stdlib probe in docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md appendix A (adds a tool on bump or 6 s later, logs every request, never discloses the new tool name). 'ddflow mcp probe-client <harness>' writes the client table row (honours|ignores, version, revision negotiated, did-it-probe-server/discover). CI runs it for each installed agent CLI in the tier-1 smoke list (agent-compat) with a dummy prompt and a cheap model; missing CLI/key = unavailable, never pass. Cells still UNKNOWN: codex, gemini, qwen, kimi, opencode, cursor, copilot cli, antigravity, grok build, windsurf, amp, droid. Overlaps RM-client-probes (long-op timeouts): share the harness, keep separate results. Warn: kilo run uploads a session share URL by default.
data.title: Per-client list_changed probe: ddflow mcp probe-client and a CI matrix over installed agent CLIs

Spawn the shim as a client would, run calls, swap to a fixture worker version: (a) digest unchanged -> soft, same connection, new worker pid; (b) tool added/removed -> soft with list_changed seen by a scripted client that honours it, hard for one that does not; (c) in-flight call across the swap completes; (d) worker crash -> restart, typed error, connection alive; (e) shim protocol bump -> hard. Optional live case against the claude CLI behind an env flag (the scratchpad probe).

Add one case per class: unchanged digest; additive under an honouring client; additive under an ignoring client (hard + notice); same swap with facade mode on (soft).

data.summary: SU-client-matrix is a docs-only research task but was created kind=task (ddflow_task_add has no kind parameter; 'ddflow update' has no --kind; tags=doc does not select the doc pipeline). complete then refuses: 'required gate(s) not passed: unit_tests (skipped)' although 'gate skip --reason' was the documented way past a gate. Add kind to the MCP tool and to update, and let a recorded skip with a reason satisfy a required gate or say so at skip time.
data.title: A task's kind cannot be set via MCP task_add or changed with update; skipped unit_tests then blocks complete
